subject.title: Stuck-session liveness monitor misclassifies healthy processing runs as stale during event-loop stalls

question: Should OpenClaw change the processing/no-activeWorkKind recovery policy now, or require live measurement proving that healthy active runs can lose activity bookkeeping during event-loop stalls?
rationale: Current source shows the reported fallthrough, but current tests intentionally depend on that recovery behavior and the report labels the healthy-run abort chain as likely rather than confirmed.

options.title: Require proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open for a targeted reproduction or measurement that shows a healthy active run reaching stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run before changing recovery semantics.

options.title: Patch classifier now
options.body: Approve a narrow code change that treats processing/no-activeWorkKind as observe-only or long-running, accepting the need to redesign the existing stale-processing recovery tests.

options.title: Fold into broader liveness work
options.body: Track this as part of the adjacent event-loop and stuck-session recovery cluster instead of handling this classifier edge separately.

recommendation.title: Require proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for a targeted reproduction or measurement that shows a healthy active run reaching stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run before changing recovery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownerless-lane recovery work makes them the best routing candidate for deciding whether this recovery policy should change before live proof.
